purpose: Fosphenytoin is used to stop or prevent seizures, especially in emergency situations. It is also used to control seizures during or after brain surgery. Doctors may use it when a patient cannot take seizure medicine by mouth.
how_it_works: Once fosphenytoin enters your body, it quickly converts into another medicine called phenytoin. Phenytoin works by calming down overactive electrical signals in your brain that cause seizures. Think of it like a circuit breaker that stops the electrical storm happening in your brain.
common_side_effects: You may feel dizzy, drowsy, or unsteady on your feet. Some people experience a burning, tingling, or itching sensation, especially in the groin area, during the injection. Nausea, headache, blurred or double vision, and low blood pressure are also common.
warnings: This medicine must be given by a healthcare professional in a medical setting because it can cause serious heart problems and dangerously low blood pressure if given too fast. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, as it can harm an unborn baby. Also tell your doctor about all your other medications, since fosphenytoin interacts with many drugs. Do not stop this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor.
typical_dosing: Fosphenytoin is given by injection into a vein (IV) or into a muscle (IM) by a nurse or doctor — you will not take this one at home. The dose is based on your weight and the type of seizure being treated. Your medical team will carefully calculate and monitor your dose.
